solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notice about shelter: man with a daughter like a dormouse?

indicators.note: the word for notice goes round the word for shelter, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: to spy something is to notice or spot it
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
he is the pronoun for a man
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone spots a notice about a refuge while a man and his daughter doze like a dormouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the dormouse is the proverbial sleeper, so one 'like a dormouse' is a drowsy person, the answer being a noun for such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse in Alice is forever nodding off, so a drowsy, dozing person resembles one.

clue.text: All quiet at the oil well?

parts.note: the sum is the whole amount, all of it
P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Everything goes silent at the oil field.
explanation.definitionFit: In a car engine, the oil collects in a reservoir at the bottom of the crankcase, whimsically an oil well.

clue.text: Nearly middle rank

indicators.note: middle here asks for the inside of the word Nearly, its first and last letters shed

explanation.surface: Someone holds a rank that is almost in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle rank' reads as one phrase, a mid-level grade; split it, and 'middle' takes the core of 'Nearly' while 'rank' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a nobleman of a particular title, a rank in the British peerage.

clue.text: Disturbed his partner, first century BC

indicators.note: disturbed means these letters are churned up and set out anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, as in Charles I, the first
C is the abbreviation for century, also the Roman hundred

explanation.surface: His partner was upset in the first century before Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first century' looks like a date phrase; it is two separate pieces, I and C, mixed into the anagram with HIS PARTNER.
explanation.definitionFit: BC stands for before Christ, describing anything from the era preceding the Christian one.

clue.text: A student prince coming first with authorised food

indicators.note: coming first says the prince's name is placed ahead of the other two pieces

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
L for learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A student and a prince arrive first, bringing approved food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming first' tells you the prince goes ahead of A and the student, so HAL leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat prepared according to Islamic law is permitted, that is sanctioned for Muslims to eat.

clue.text: Chasm in island followed by a country in Africa

parts.note: an abyss is a deep chasm
I is the abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: A deep chasm on an island is followed by a trek to an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by' just keeps the pieces in order. Abyssinia is the old name for Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the historic name of the Ethiopian empire in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Bit (say) of roadside

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken and we enter a word sounding the same

parts.note: a curb is a chain or strap on a horse's bit, and the bit itself curbs the horse

explanation.surface: A small bit, so to speak, of the edge of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised stone edging of a pavement runs along the side of the road.

clue.text: Departure from country turning into mirage

indicators.note: turning means the letters are spun round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Leaving one's homeland turns out to be an illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving your native land to settle abroad is the act of moving out of a country.

clue.text: Wait a minute, as Christopher Robin might have mentioned?

definitions.meaning: a polite request for patience, asking someone to pause briefly

definitions.text: as Christopher Robin might have mentioned?
definitions.meaning: Christopher Robin's friend was Winnie-the-Pooh, a bear, so he might say the phrase meaning the bear accompanies him

explanation.surface: A request to be patient for a moment, as a boy with a teddy might put it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday plea to be patient for a moment, read literally as a bear being with the speaker.

clue.text: Music hall star presents fairy in my old play

indicators.note: in puts the fairy's name inside the rearranged letters
play means the letters are moved about loosely

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Ariel is the airy spirit in Shakespeare's The Tempest

explanation.surface: A music hall artiste puts on a sprite in a dated production of mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a stage work but signals the rearrangement, and 'presents' is only a link. Marie Lloyd was a famous British music hall singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Lloyd was the most celebrated singer of the Victorian and Edwardian variety stage.

clue.text: Opera star greatly wanting comeback

indicators.note: comeback means the word comes back, read from its end

parts.note: to be avid is to want something greatly, to be eager

explanation.surface: A soprano is keen to return to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Silver isn't angelic

definitions.meaning: silver is not equal in worth to the yellow precious metal, falling short of it
well behaved, like a model child

explanation.surface: Silver is not saintly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: silver is not of equal value to the more precious metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A child described this way is perfectly behaved, a little angel.

clue.text: Ill-gotten wealth covers irregular starts, which is fatal for the camel

definitions.text: which is fatal for the camel

indicators.note: covers means one set of letters is wrapped around the other
ill-gotten suggests something got badly, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: irregular means the letters are set out in no fixed order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ill-gotten riches hide some uneven beginnings, which finishes off the camel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the proverb of the straw that breaks the camel's back; 'which is' joins it as a relative clause standing for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says one final straw added to the load breaks the camel's back.

clue.text: No hard shoulder? Tell Rod

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone, telling tales
a verge is a rod or staff carried as a symbol of office, as by a verger

explanation.surface: A motorist asks whether there is no hard shoulder and is told to ask Rod.
explanation.walkthrough: A hard shoulder is the paved strip at the side of a British motorway; a grassy one is the soft alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of grass beside a road is a soft edge rather than a paved hard shoulder.

clue.text: Vacancies in top jobs in foreign land going to some magnate

parts.note: terre is French for land

indicators.note: some means only part of the word magnate is used, the three letters at its centre

explanation.surface: Gaps at the top in an overseas land go to a tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' just joins the pieces. Interregna are gaps between reigns or office-holders.
explanation.definitionFit: Interregna are periods between two rulers or holders of a post when the throne or office is empty.

clue.text: Performance, covert if extraordinary

definitions.meaning: a performance or interpretation of a piece of music or a role
extraordinary ... is the covert state transfer of a suspect abroad for interrogation

explanation.surface: A show that is secret if remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer's version of a song is their interpretation or performance of it.

clue.text: Lopsidedness of an alembic, maybe

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters might be put in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tilt in a distiller's still, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of balance between the two sides makes something lopsided.

clue.text: Group getting back to holding and so on

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled run is read in reverse
holding means the first word encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
etc is short for et cetera, meaning and so on

explanation.surface: A band gets back to holding on, and so forth.
explanation.walkthrough: TO holding ETC makes TETCO, and 'back' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of eight performers or things forms a musical or other group.

clue.text: Trouble in Australia took place without the Poms

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: sat is took a place, as in a seat
Poms is Australian slang for the English, so to an English setter they are we

explanation.surface: There was trouble Down Under when something happened without the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside. Sweat as trouble is mainly met in the Australian 'no sweat', no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian usage sweat means bother or difficulty, as in no worries, no bother.

clue.text: Pig meets fate having taken in royal directors

parts.note: a boar is a male pig

indicators.note: having taken in means the word for fate absorbs the letter

parts.note: doom is one's fate or destiny
R is short for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A pig meets its end after taking in royalty on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meets' just joins the pieces; the definition is 'directors' standing for where they meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The company board of directors meets in this room, so the room stands for them.

clue.text: Inconstancy in operating abrasive lens

indicators.note: operating means the letters are worked on and reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An abrasive lens in use gives inconsistent results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: the definition is in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Being changeable from moment to moment is the opposite of steady, unchanging constancy.

clue.text: Scottish refusal to 6 birthmarks

parts.note: nae is Scots for no
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Scot says no to six birthmarks.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to the clue numbered 6, but here it is just the number six.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevus is the medical word for a mole or birthmark; this is its plural.

clue.text: Mercian king of footballers?

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, the English football body

explanation.surface: A king of Mercia rules over footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was the eighth-century king of Mercia in the English Midlands, famed for Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia from 757 to 796.

clue.text: Network shows girl missing home

indicators.note: missing means a piece is taken out of the name

parts.note: Ingrid is a girl's name
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A network reveals a girl absent from home.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a lattice or network, as of lines, streets or electricity cables.

clue.text: Fashionable temper?

definitions.meaning: in fashion, so the word alone stands for the craze

explanation.surface: Is bad temper in fashion?
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is a burst of temper, and the latest craze is all the fashion.

clue.text: In process of sale found freer option

indicators.note: option suggests choosing a different arrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A buyer finds a freer choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A property with an accepted bid but not yet sold is subject to that offer.

clue.text: Cheese produced in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: made means produced

explanation.surface: Cheese is made during an economic downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a round Dutch cheese in red wax.

clue.text: In arrears as cough should be?

definitions.meaning: politeness says you cough with your hand in front of your mouth, the cough kept out of sight

explanation.surface: Late with payments, as manners say a cough should be covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being late with payments or work leaves one behind schedule, overdue.
